transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey, Doc. Yeah, well... I guess what finally got me in here is that over these last few months, my mind just keeps jumping all over the place. I drive a truck for a living, right? And lately, every little thing catches my attention. Every CB chirp, every fuel price sign... which, by the way, did you see what diesel is going for down on I-95? It's absolute highway robbery. Used to be you could fill up the rig without taking out a second mortgage, but now... I don't know how the independent guys are even staying afloat out there. I actually had this whole new idea the other day about how they ought to restructure the fuel surcharges, just chewing on it for a hundred miles. 

But anyway, yeah, my mind just jumps to all that stuff—the signs, the radio, whatever new idea pops into my head—and I end up missing details I normally never miss. Like, I'll completely overlook a client’s delivery note, or I'll totally forget who I promised to call back. It's just not like me to drop the ball like that, you know?
Would you say you've been like this—easily distracted, mind jumping around—since you were a kid, or is this a new change that started just in the last few months?

No, no, not since I was a kid. I was always pretty sharp, you know? Kept my logs tight, never missed a beat. It's really just a new thing. I'd say it's been going on for about seven months now, right around the time my daughter moved back home. I started trying to keep everything steady for her, you know, because she had this whole messy breakup with her boyfriend. The guy was just a real piece of work, honestly. I told her from the very beginning that he was no good, but kids, they just have to learn the hard way. 

So she packs up her little car and comes back, and I swear, the suspension on that thing is completely shot. I keep telling her I need to take it into the shop because driving on these county roads with bad struts is just asking to end up in a ditch. I actually know a guy over at the tire shop off Route 9 who owes me a favor from way back, so I should probably give him a ring this week before the weather turns. He used to run a rig himself before he messed up his shoulder. 

But yeah, she moved back into her old room, and I've just been trying to keep the peace and keep the house steady. Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the distraction stuff. Yeah, about seven months.

Have you ever had a period in the past—lasting a couple of weeks or more—where you felt unusually depressed, low, or lacking energy, or on the other hand, unusually elevated, energetic, or 'high' before this current episode?

No, I don't think so. I've always been pretty even-keeled, you know? Just putting in the miles, doing my job. I mean, sure, everybody gets a little tired after a long haul, especially when you're stuck in that dead-stop traffic on 81. I swear, they've been doing construction on that same stretch of highway for, what, five years now? It's ridiculous. You sit there burning fuel, the AC struggling to keep up because it's dead summer, and you just watch the hours tick by on your logbook. And don't even get me started on the four-wheelers trying to zip around you on the shoulder. I saw this guy in a little red sports car last week—must have been going ninety—nearly clip the jersey barrier trying to squeeze past a flatbed. Just no respect for the physics of a big rig, you know? If that flatbed had tapped his brakes, that little car would have been a tin can. 

I actually used to have a red car way back in the day, a Mustang. Loved that thing. Wish I'd never sold it, but you know how it goes when you start a family. Had to get something sensible. 

But yeah, no, I've never really had any big highs or lows like you're talking about. Just normal tired, I guess.

Over these past seven months, have you noticed your mood itself feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or extra irritable—more than just being distracted—like feeling on top of the world or unusually short-tempered?

Well, yeah, honestly. For months now, I've just been... I don't know, either way too fired up, like I'm on top of the world and everything is going to work out perfectly no matter what, or I'm just snapping at everyone over the smallest stuff. Like at home, or out in the yard. Speaking of the yard, I finally got around to fixing that old riding mower. The carburetor was completely gunked up. You wouldn't believe the ethanol in the gas these days, it just eats away at the seals. I was telling the guy at the hardware store about it—he's this older fella, used to work on small engines down in Florida before he moved up here. He said you gotta use the non-ethanol fuel if you want those things to last, which makes sense, but it's like a dollar more a gallon, and you have to drive all the way out to the marina just to find a pump that sells it. 

I actually thought about getting a couple of jerry cans and just stocking up, but then you gotta worry about storing it, and my garage is already packed with all my daughter's boxes she brought back. I swear she kept every notebook from high school. But yeah, anyway, I've just been really short-tempered lately, or just way too pumped up. It's really not my usual way to be like this.

Even if it wasn't diagnosed or didn't seem like a big deal at the time, have you ever had another stretch of days or weeks—at any point earlier in your life—where your mood or energy felt distinctly different from your usual self, either much lower or much higher, before these past seven months?

No, really, I've racked my brain and I just don't think so. I mean, I've always been pretty steady. You gotta be steady when you're driving a rig, you know? You can't be flying off the handle or getting all down in the dumps when you're hauling 80,000 pounds of freight. It's a lot of responsibility. I remember this one time I was hauling a load of frozen chickens down to Atlanta. Middle of July, hotter than a match head, and the reefer unit on the trailer starts acting up. The temperature gauge was just creeping up, creeping up. I had to pull over at this little truck stop off I-75—one of those mom-and-pop places that still has the good chicken fried steak—and try to troubleshoot the damn thing. 

Turns out it was just a loose belt, but man, I was sweating bullets thinking about having to explain a whole trailer of spoiled chicken to the dispatcher. Dispatchers, they don't care if it's a mechanical issue, they just want the load there on time. My old dispatcher, Jerry, he was a real hard-ass about that stuff. He actually retired last year and bought an RV. Said he was gonna drive around the country with his wife, which is funny because he spent thirty years sitting at a desk yelling at guys who were driving around the country. 

But no, to answer your question, before these last seven months, I've never had anything like this happen. Just been my normal self.
Over these past seven months, have you noticed that you need much less sleep than usual—like feeling fully rested after only a few hours—without feeling tired the next day?

Yeah, actually, that's exactly how it's been. Most nights I sleep maybe three or four hours, tops. Then I’m up way before daylight, just feeling totally ready to roll instead of worn out. It's weird because normally, if I don't get my solid seven hours, I'm dragging. But lately, I'm just up and at 'em. I'll make a pot of coffee—I got this new percolator, actually. One of those old-school stovetop ones? The drip machines just don't get it hot enough, you know? My buddy Dave told me about it. He's a mechanic over at the Peterbilt dealership. Great guy, but he drinks his coffee black as tar, like, leaves the spoon standing straight up in the mug. He says it puts hair on your chest, but I don't know, my stomach can't handle it like that anymore. Gotta have a little creamer in there. 

Anyway, Dave was the one who helped me swap out the alternator on my rig a couple years back when it died right in the middle of a snowstorm in Ohio. Man, that was a mess. The snow was coming down so hard you couldn't see the hood ornament. But yeah, I've just been waking up after three hours and feeling like I could run a marathon or drive straight through to California.
